page.layout: One printed page. Running head at the top centre. Below it, a short italic verse epigraph, then a centred title in capitals with a subtitle line. Then the main body, a verse passage in italic with an initial D. No marginal notes. Catchword "Illa" at the lower right, below the last line.

l.i: Tam prompte lacrymis pauefacto ex pectore fusi /
Restinguat iram numinis, /
Quam siccos retinens oculos Vetus illa rebellis /
Sese Sion pessum dedit.
Diuinum si quid mortalibus illa reliquit /
Humani labes generis, caligine caca /
Quae mentis lucem inuoluit, fecitque voluntas /
In vitium miserè praeceps vt tota feratur, /
Tunc quoque quum recta ferri ratione videtur: /
Id tibi, magne Plato, veluti diuinitus omne /
Collatum quondam si quis fortasse negarit, /
Quid non ille idem perfricta fronte negarit? /
Et tamen haec quidnam lux est, nisi qualis opaca /
Illustrat noctem Lunae sublustris imago? /
Nos igitur seruata tibi haec caelestia dona /
Miremur, liceatque etiam spectare, diuque, /
Versare, ac nostris aptare quoque sensibus illa: /
Dummodo quae nobis lux caelo affulsit ab alto, /
Lux exprompta sinu Veri quae numinis
Vna, / Errantes mundi in pelago nos Vna gubernet. /
Asti ego quàm vellem, decus immortale Sophorum, /
Istius pariter lucis te dona tulisse, /
Vere vt diuini ferres cognomina vatis! /
Irrita sed quando sunt nostra haec vota, quod Vnu[?] /
Iam superest, istud munus tibi gratulor ingens, / Illa

page.notes: The initial D is a large woodcut-style letter, joined to "iuinum" as "Diuinum". Several words of the verse are blurred or ambiguous in the scan: "Vna" (lines 15 and 18), "Vnu" and "Sophorum" are read from the scan with doubt, and "Vnu[?]" marks the least certain. The long-s glyph has been written as plain s. The small mark at the foot centre is not text.
